title: Large Language Models in Education: Foundations, Customization, Applications, and Responsible Use
extended_summary:
This chapter/paper provides a conceptual and technical overview of large language models (LLMs) in education, with emphasis on how they work, why they matter, and what limits and risks accompany their use. It explains the Transformer architecture, scaling laws, pre-training, instruction tuning, and alignment, then connects these foundations to educational uses such as tutoring, content generation, lesson planning, assessment creation, rubric design, differentiated texts, and simulated practice scenarios.

The customization section focuses on how educational institutions can adapt LLMs through prompt engineering, few-shot prompting, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT). It discusses these methods as ways to align model behavior with curriculum standards, reasoning transparency, age appropriateness, and institutional privacy requirements. The chapter also distinguishes between proprietary and open-source models, arguing that the choice affects cost, privacy, transparency, and deployment feasibility.

The paper is not an empirical study of a specific classroom intervention; rather, it is a framework-oriented discussion aimed at educators, developers, and institutions considering LLM adoption. It concludes that LLMs have strong potential as teacher co-pilots and scalable educational infrastructure, but their use must be cautious because of hallucinations, bias, finite context windows, privacy risks, and environmental and financial costs.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: General-purpose large language models / generative AI systems that can tutor, generate content, provide feedback, and be customized via prompting, retrieval, and fine-tuning.
identified_tools.use_case: This chapter discusses LLMs as a class of teacher- and student-facing generative AI tools for education, including tutoring, assessment support, lesson planning, feedback generation, and differentiated content creation. It does not evaluate a specific deployed product or report empirical results.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/theoretical chapter rather than an empirical study. It explains LLM capabilities, customization methods, and deployment considerations, but reports no study design, sample, or measured outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The chapter argues that LLMs may reduce teacher workload and support tutoring, assessment, and lesson planning, but it provides no direct outcome data or effect sizes. As a framework paper, any impact claims are speculative and not empirically demonstrated here.
